nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many alternative currency schemes are estimated to exist around the world?
nodes.answer: Approximately 5000 schemes are estimated to exist in over 50 countries.
nodes.paragraph: (Fare and Ahmed 2018, p. 1). As we discuss further in this section, the English acronym CCs is often used as a meta-name to describe complementary currencies or community currencies (Blanc 2011). While it is difficult to account for all of the alternative currencies around the world, primarily because a number of them are not known outside their community or they are not formally studied (Fare 2016), estimations suggest there are approximately 5000 schemes in over 50 countries (Blanc 2018). The vast majority of contemporary alternative cur - rencies began to appear around the world by the end of the 1980s. Moreover, four years after the creation of Bitcoin, there were more than 600 cryptocurrencies in 2013 (Hile- man 2013 ), a number estimated at more than 7500 as of November 20211 reflecting an impressive growth. At the end of the 2000s, in numerous countries the observation of the acceleration of environmental and social crises and the anticipation of the decline of fossil fuels and their cli- matic impacts saw the emergence of the Transition Towns Movement2 with, among other things, the creation of local currencies as primordial tools towards the re-localisation of the economy of communities (North 2013; Stamm 2021).
